See also: acker and Äcker

English

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Received Pronunciation) IPA(key): /ˈækə/
  • (General American) IPA(key): /ˈækɚ/
  • Rhymes: -ækə(ɹ)

Proper noun

[edit]

Acker

  1. An English topographical surname from Old English from Old English æcer (“field”).
  2. A German topographical surname from German from Old High German ackar (“field”).
  3. nickname from the Somerset slang for "friend" or "mate", e.g. Acker Bilk

Derived terms

[edit]
  • Ackerian

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Crake, Kacer, crake, creak

German

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • Aker (obsolete)

Etymology

[edit]

From Middle High German acker, from Old High German ackar (“field”), from Proto-West Germanic *akr.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈʔakɐ/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Germany (Berlin)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -akɐ

Noun

[edit]

Acker m (strong, genitive Ackers, plural Äcker, diminutive Äckerchen n or Äckerlein n)

  1. field (wide, open space used to grow crops)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of Acker [masculine, strong]
singular plural
indef. def. noun def. noun
nominative ein der Acker die Äcker
genitive eines des Ackers der Äcker
dative einem dem Acker den Äckern
accusative einen den Acker die Äcker

Hunsrik

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

    Inherited from Middle High German acker.[1]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈaka/
    • Rhymes: -aka
    • Syllabification: Ac‧ker

    Noun

    [edit]

    Acker m (plural Ecker)

    1. acre (unit of surface area)
